claim: A `change-file` naming a generated file keeps no edit and answers as though it kept one. The call exits nought, prints the line that says the edits are kept, and prints no path. `akasha change list` afterwards shows nothing for that path. Nothing tells the caller the edit was refused or why.

evidence:
Measured 2026-09-10 taking `file-property/worked` away once no page type stated it.

The removal of `page/type/properties/worked.file-property.ts` is refused by `import-not-left-hanging`: "`page/type/page-type.page-type.types.ts` imports `page/type/properties/worked.file-property.ts`, and `page/type/properties/worked.file-property.ts` holds no body after". That importer is generated: the landing writes it again from the page type's own properties.

The finding `an-act-is-taken-away-only-after-a-hand-edit-the-landing-discards` records the way through: hand-edit the generated body first so the removal drafts, and let the landing throw that edit away. That way is closed here. Two `change-file` calls over `page/type/page-type.page-type.types.ts`, each with an `old` block matching the body `akasha change show` prints, both answered "the edits are kept" and named no path. `akasha change list` then held only the two edits over `page/type/page-type.page-type.ts`, and `akasha change show` printed the types file unchanged.

The removal landed at 56b61004b7 once the guard was taught to skip an importer a generator owns, so that way through is no longer wanted there. The silent keep is untouched: a `change-file` over a generated file still answers as though it kept an edit.

The way to close it is not a refusal inside `withheld`. A refactor rewriting an import specifier answers a replace on every generated `.types.ts` that specifier reaches, and those replaces are dropped here and written again by `typesFor` at landing, so refusing would stop every rename. The drop is load-bearing.

Saying it out loud instead wants a channel that is not there. `Answer` in `change/modules/answer/change-answer.module.types.ts` carries edits and a refusal and no advisory text. `Reached` in `change/modules/shadow/change-shadow.module.code.ts` is named in three files and built in five places, so a third field is cheap to declare, but 42 of the 102 calls to `reach` answer `(await reach(...)).said` and drop the rest, and two more repackage the pair into a local type, so reading that field is a change at every call site. The `said` channel the composing runner uses is landing-side: `preparing` builds it from the change rows, and the withheld edit is gone by then.

The judging belongs at the act rather than at the reach. A person aims `change-file`, `append-lines` or an `add-property-` act at one path, and that path is knowable before any reach runs. A refactor reaching a generated file among many others is a different case and wants no such judging.
